patients.summary: Former construction foreman on Medicare disability with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and PAD who joins in 2020 as a heavy smoker. Over six years he is diagnosed with severe emphysema, right renal artery stenosis, a benign tracheal papilloma, an ascending colon adenoma with iron deficiency, and stage IIIB squamous NSCLC that progresses with SVC syndrome and brain metastases; an SMA aneurysm is repaired along the way.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

53 y/o man transferring care after his previous internist retired. Lives in Easthampton with his wife. Was a construction foreman, out on medical leave now and on Medicare disability with a supplemental plan.

HTN: about 9 years, on HCTZ 25 the whole time, says it has always been fine. No home cuff.
Lipids: atorvastatin 40, been on it 6 or 7 years, no muscle complaints.
PAD: last year his legs started cramping in the calves walking from the truck to the job site, worse on the left. Prior doctor did leg artery testing and told him it was blockage; started baby aspirin. Today he gets about two blocks before the left calf makes him stop, rests a minute and it lets go. No rest pain, no foot sores.

PSH: inguinal hernia repair at 45.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father died of lung cancer at 60. Mother has high BP, 77 and doing well. Uncle on dad's side had colon cancer.
SH: smokes, roughly 2 packs a day since he was 16 or 17. Has never seriously tried to stop. Drinks once or twice a month at most. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, no palpitations, no dyspnea he'll admit to, no cough. Bowels regular, no blood.

Exam: well-appearing, smells of smoke. BP and vitals per flowsheet. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, a bit distant. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed groin scar. Feet warm, DP pulses faint on the L, palpable on the R; no ulcers. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypertension, controlled on HCTZ. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel.
3. PAD with stable claudication. Continue ASA and statin. Walking program. Main thing that would help his legs is stopping smoking, told him that plainly.
4. Tobacco: 2 ppd. Not ready to set a date. Offered patch or varenicline; he'll think.
5. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screen today. Colon screening offered, colonoscopy or stool card; he isn't interested right now. Flu shot given L deltoid.
6. Sending for old records.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, your blood work from Monday is back. Kidney function, potassium, sugar, liver tests and blood count are all normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative, so those are done for good. Cholesterol on the atorvastatin is in an acceptable range for now; we'll keep the same dose. The one thing I'd change is the cigarettes, and I'm here when you're ready.

documents.title: Records from prior internal medicine office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 41 pages by fax from the patient's previous internist (practice closed; records custodian sent). Abstracted:
- Hypertension listed from 2011, HCTZ 25 mg throughout, office BPs mostly 120s-130s/70s-80s.
- Hyperlipidemia, atorvastatin 40 mg started 2014.
- 2019 note: calf claudication L>R, lower extremity arterial study ordered; result page not included in the packet. Aspirin 81 started.
- Inguinal hernia repair 2012.
- Tdap 04/2016.
- Repeated smoking cessation counseling, declined.
Scanned to media, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic refill request from his pharmacy for HCTZ 25 and atorvastatin 40, old prescriber no longer active. Rewrote both under our PCP, 90-day supply with 3 refills. Aspirin is OTC.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV + problem visit

Health risk assessment reviewed with him: lives with wife in a single-level house, no falls, no hearing complaints, drives. Independent with self-care and errands. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. No advance directive yet; gave him the health care proxy form to fill out with his wife.

Problem: L calf claudication is worse over the winter. Now about one block before he has to stop. R leg only aches with hills. No rest pain, no wounds. Still smoking 2 ppd, "down a little" he says.

Exam: BP ok. L DP/PT not palpable today, R DP faint. Feet warm, cap refill brisk, no skin breakdown. Lungs clear but distant. Heart RRR.

A/P
- PAD, L > R, progressing on aspirin/statin. He wants to know if something can be done, he likes walking. Referral to vascular surgery.
- HTN controlled, continue HCTZ.
- Tobacco: talked again. Not ready.
- Colon screening: declined again.
- COVID vaccine: he's eligible next month, plans to get it at the pharmacy.

Next visit in 6 months.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Saw vascular in the spring and had a stent put in the artery of his left thigh in late May, outpatient through the groin, home same day. We never got anything from them. He thinks he was on a second blood thinner for a while after but has run out and nobody refilled it; he's only on the aspirin now. Walking much better, can do the loop around his neighborhood without stopping. Smoking unchanged.

Meds as listed. No new problems.

O: vitals per flowsheet. L groin without hematoma or bruit. L DP now palpable. Lungs clear, prolonged expiration. RRR.

A/P
- PAD s/p L femoral stent 5/2021, symptoms much improved. Continue aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 40. Records request to vascular today so we know what was done and what follow-up they want.
- HTN fine. BMP.
- Flu shot today.
- Smoking: same conversation. He knows.

documents.title: Outside records follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called vascular surgery office re: records request faxed 9/27. They say it was sent; nothing has arrived here. Re-faxed request with signed release. Will check again in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Outside records follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Still no records from vascular. Second request sent. Closing this task; PCP aware.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request, HCTZ 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg, 90 days x 3. Last visit 9/27, BMP normal. Approved per protocol.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Interval: COVID booster at the pharmacy in November. Legs doing well since the stent. Still 2 ppd. When asked, says he gets winded faster than he used to with carrying things or a flight of stairs, has been that way for some months, figures it's age and the cigarettes. No cough, no chest pain, no leg swelling. Doesn't want testing for it now.

Functional: independent, no falls, hearing and vision fine, driving. HCP form completed, wife is agent, copy scanned.
PHQ-2 0. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs with mildly decreased breath sounds throughout, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. Pulses: L DP palpable.

Plan:
- Breathlessness: told him I'd like breathing tests if this keeps up; he'd rather wait. Revisit at next visit.
- Tobacco: strongly advised quitting.
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months with the nurse.
- Colonoscopy/FIT: still no.
- Fasting lipids and CMP today. Vascular records never came; closed the request.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for second Shingrix. Tolerated first dose with a day of tiredness. Given 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Series complete.

documents.body: can I get in sometime in the next few weeks. breathing has been getting worse, nothing urgent

documents.title: RE: appointment

documents.body: Hi Sean, you're booked Monday 9/19 at 10:00 with the doctor. If your breathing gets worse before then, call us and we'll see you sooner.

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: getting short of breath.

HPI: Breathing has slowly gotten worse over about the last year. Now has to stop to catch his breath before he's gone several blocks; used to blame getting older. Wife has an albuterol inhaler and he's been borrowing it some days, thinks it helps a little. Denies cough, denies phlegm, no fever, no chest pain. Legs are fine since the stent. Still smoking about 2 packs a day.

Exam: speaks in full sentences. Lungs: quiet breath sounds throughout, prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No edema today. SpO2 per flowsheet.

A/P
Progressive exertional dyspnea in a 55 y/o with roughly 80 pack-years. Most likely obstructive lung disease. Full PFTs with lung volumes and a pulmonology consult. Told him not to keep using his wife's inhaler; we'll get him his own once we know what this is.
The best thing for his lungs is to stop smoking now. For the first time he says he's ready. Discussed patch/gum and varenicline; he wants to try on his own first, setting a quit date in two weeks. Will call him.
Flu shot today.

documents.title: Quit check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt as planned. He stopped smoking a week ago today, cold turkey, threw out the cartons. Irritable but managing, chewing sunflower seeds. Declines nicotine replacement for now. PFTs are booked for 10/24 and pulmonary for 10/31. Encouraged; told him to call if he wants patches.

reports.text: Complete pulmonary function study: spirometry before and after bronchodilator, lung volumes by plethysmography. Effort and reproducibility acceptable. FEV1/FVC ratio 55%, reduced. Total lung capacity elevated. Residual volume elevated. Findings indicate an obstructive ventilatory defect with hyperinflation and air trapping.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive defect with hyperinflation and air trapping; FEV1/FVC 55%.

medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath

documents.title: Pulmonary Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 10/31/2022
Referred by: primary care

Reason: shortness of breath, review of pulmonary function testing.

Mr. Hennessey is a 55-year-old former construction foreman who describes a year of slowly progressive breathlessness. At this point several city blocks is his limit before he must stop. He has no cough and brings up no sputum. He has been using his wife's albuterol inhaler intermittently with some relief.

History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral arterial disease with a femoral stent. Hernia repair at 45.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with lung cancer, died at 60; mother hypertensive; paternal uncle with colon cancer.
Social: 80 pack-years; he stopped smoking about four weeks ago. Rare alcohol.

Examination: breath sounds diminished on both sides with a hyperresonant percussion note. Barrel-shaped chest with increased anteroposterior dimension. He uses accessory muscles even sitting quietly. Pulmonic component of S2 is loud. Mild edema at both ankles.

Pulmonary function (10/24/2022): FEV1/FVC 55%. TLC and RV both increased, consistent with hyperinflation and gas trapping.

Impression: severe emphysema, upper lobe predominant, in a heavy former smoker.

Recommendations:
1. Tiotropium soft-mist inhaler, 2 inhalations once daily.
2. Albuterol HFA 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed; he should stop using his wife's.
3. Congratulated on quitting; continued abstinence is essential.
4. Return to pulmonary clinic as needed or with any change.

Thank you for this referral.
Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Pharmacy fill history
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy called to verify an outside prescriber for a 90-day supply on file. Fill history shows new tiotropium inhaler and albuterol HFA dated 10/31, written by pulmonology. We have no pulmonary note yet. Called patient: he says the lung doctor told him he has emphysema and to use the new inhaler every morning. Added both inhalers to his list as outside meds. Requested the consult note.

You should hear from the pharmacy in a few days. Keep using it every morning in the meantime; you have enough from the first fill.
